[b]A DEAD DEMOCRACY[/b]

[list][sub]Today marks 30 years since President Cameron Redding came to power, in a decisive 1995 election that would cost Chaltania it's democracy. After promising pro-worker policies following a string of capitalist presidents throughout the 70s and 80s, Redding would easily achieve victory, and would soon enact his promises. Things went well throughout his first term, and he would be elected once again in 2000 for a second term. However, while the Chaltanian constitution only allowed for two terms, he had been seeking for the passage of a constitution amendment that would allow for a third term, and this was seeming likely for a while, until everything went south for him.[/sub]

[sub]An economic collapse in 2004 and a scandal that exposed him for bribing corporations for support in political campaigns that he had been publicly threatening to bring down destroyed his reputation, and by 2005, the people had selected a new candidate in order to get rid of Redding and leave him in the past. But just days before the inauguration of the new president, the nation was shocked to hear that a small faction of pro-Redding loyalists in the military who supported his policies stormed multiple government buildings across the capital of Innosene. Before long, Redding stood before national television, announcing the dissolution of the country's parliament due to what he claimed was the "purposeful rigging of the election", announcing a state of emergency with it. Although he promised to soon end this state of emergency within days, those days turned into weeks, weeks turned into months, months into years, and years into decades.[/sub]

[sub]Nowadays, Chaltania continues to be ruled with an iron fist. In 2007, the country would adopt a new constitution that basically handed Redding all the power he wanted. Any sign of protests were brutally put down, and the faction of pro-Redding military officers that initially overthrew the government expanded to become Chaltania's secret police, also known as the Bureau of Domestic Stability, or the BDS. Redding himself, who just turned 68, presides over the nation. Anything he says, goes, and sham elections are held every five years to at least try to appear "democratic". Redding's anti-globalist and anti-liberalist agendas has put Chaltania at odds with the international community, which is moving closer and closer together as alliances are formed and global trade expands.[/sub][/list]

[b]Ocean hijacking[/b]

The Sal-Baliz corvette Rawuwf waits in the Baliwick sea for it's prey. Details of an Orphogronian uranium shipment have once again be provided to the Sal-Baliz and soon they are to be "hijacked". That was the plan anyway, but at around 10:20pm an odd vessel appeared on the foggy horizon. It first appeared as s military patrol boat, causing panic among the Sal-Baliz. Immediately missiles were fired. The missiles hit the front of the appraoching ship, causing it to begin to sink. The Rawuwf speeds towards the rapidly sinking ship in order to capture hostages, but they soon discover that the ship is a small civilian speedboat, even better. The small vessel is promptly boarded. The people on board appear to be from the ULR, possibly fishermen. They put up a small fight, but are no match for the unmerciful Sal-Baliz soldiers. The personnel of the boat is rounded up, a grand total of 5 people, all close friends by the looks of it. The men are made to put their hands behind their heads so that the Sal-Baliz can make a broadcast. An old camera from the late 80s is used to film the helpless fishermen, who all have multiple rifles pointed to their heads.

[i]"To the ULR government, these are your people and if you want them back I suggest you comply with what we are about to ask. First, we want your word that you will not trade or be involved in any way with THEP or it's members. Secondly, you will end the persecution of Muslims within your borders, or face the might of Al-Qadi. Third and finally, you shall send us 200,000 barrels of oil and a sum of 1,000,000,000 tabuhts immediately. Comply and your people will return safely, disobey and they will die, simple. You have 72 hours."[/i]

The recording cuts out and is broadcast directly to the ULR government. Whilst the Sal-Baliz wait for a response, the hostages are being transported back into Sal-Baliz territory and being held in a prison cell. Another ship has been deployed to receive the uranium.
